title: Assembly Line Balancing & Layout Optimisation
challenge: Uneven work allocation across 14 sub-assembly stations caused severe line starvation, operator idle time, and low daily throughput.
clientSituation: Excessive operator movement and material handling backtracking between stations
High line balance delay causing 40% waiting time on bottleneck workstations
Congested sub-assembly area restricting forklift material feeding
Inconsistent cycle times ranging from 45 to 120 seconds per workstation
approach: Conducted Current State Value Stream Mapping (VSM) and Line Balance Audit
Executed MOST (Maynard Operation Sequence Technique) time-and-motion studies
Created Spaghetti Diagrams to track operator travel routes and material movement
Designed Yamazumi charts to redistribute work elements equally to Takt time
Developed Future State U-shaped cellular workstation layout
Simulated line flow and implemented gravity-fed material presentation chutes
implementation: Rebalanced 14 assembly workstations to a uniform 78-second Takt time pace
Installed ergonomic part presentation racks and Poka-Yoke sensor fixtures
Implemented visual line management boards and hour-by-hour production tracking
Trained shift supervisors on Standard Work auditing and Daily Management Systems

clientQuote.text: The line rebalancing and layout redesign dramatically improved production pace. We eliminated operator waiting time and achieved our highest daily throughput without adding headcount.
clientQuote.author: Operations Head, Automotive Tier-1 Manufacturer

title: Plate Mill Capacity Optimisation
challenge: Severe throughput bottlenecks at plate shearing lines and uncoordinated reheating schedules restricted total plant volume.
clientSituation: Hot rolling mill starved of reheated slabs due to uncoordinated furnace sequencing
Plate shearing line operating as severe constraint bottleneck causing slab cooling delays
WIP inventory buildup between billet casting and finishing dispatch yards
High energy consumption and furnace thickness changeover downtime
approach: Executed End-to-End Material Velocity and Bottleneck Capacity Audit
Applied Theory of Constraints (TOC) to identify physical plant bottlenecks
Modeled Drum-Buffer-Rope (DBR) schedule for furnace heating and rolling
Designed slab sequencing rules to minimize furnace thickness changes
Standardized shearing bed staging and cooling yard buffer management
implementation: Implemented Drum-Buffer-Rope scheduling software cadence for reheating furnaces
Sub-optimized non-bottleneck processes to ensure 100% feeding of hot rolling mill
Established visual buffer management indicators across cooling beds and shearing lines
Rolled out hourly bottleneck output tracking and downtime escalation routines

clientQuote.text: Pinnacle Logic identified hidden capacity in our mill that we didn't know existed. Unlocking 30% additional output without purchasing new machinery saved us crores in Capex.
clientQuote.author: General Manager - Operations, Integrated Steel Manufacturer

title: OEE & Quick Changeover Optimisation
challenge: High-runner extrusion film lines lost 12+ hours per die changeover due to disorganized tool preparation and unstandardized procedures.
clientSituation: Extrusion die setup downtime averaging 12 hours per product run
Unorganized tool locating and missing specialized wrenches during changeovers
Frequent micro-stoppages and polymer trim scrap during line restarts
Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) trapped at a low 42%
approach: Conducted video SMED (Single-Minute Exchange of Die) audit of changeover steps
Categorized changeover tasks into internal (machine stopped) and external (machine running) elements
Converted internal die pre-heating tasks into external prep activities
Designed standardized color-coded tooling carts and quick-clamping fixtures
Established visual OEE tracking boards and Autonomous Maintenance routines
implementation: Rolled out standardized SMED changeover checklists and timing sheets
Installed pre-heating stations for extrusion die tools next to production lines
Trained machine operators and maintenance crews on parallel changeover execution
Instituted 6 Big Losses downtime tracking and 5-Why root cause analysis

clientQuote.text: Reducing our die changeover time from 12 hours down to 7.4 hours gave us immense flexibility. Our OEE jumped 18% in just 90 days.
clientQuote.author: VP Operations, Flexible Packaging & Extrusion Plant

title: Workforce Productivity Improvement
challenge: Heavy casting foundry suffered from high contract headcount dependency, manual flask handling delays, and poor spatial layout.
clientSituation: High contract labor dependency causing high conversion cost inflation
Heavy manual lifting of moulding flasks resulting in worker fatigue and injuries
40% non-value-added movement due to disorganized sand moulding and pouring bays
Uneven mould setting cycle times leading to molten metal cooling losses
approach: Executed Day-In-The-Life-Of (DILO) studies for moulding crews and furnace teams
Mapped worker travel paths and ergonomics using motion economy principles
Designed low-cost pneumatic hoists and gravity chutes for flask handling (LCIA)
Redesigned moulding shop layout into cellular work bays by casting weight
Created standardized work sheets for core setting and mould assembly
implementation: Relocated core setting stations adjacent to moulding bays to eliminate travel
Installed pneumatic assist hoists for effortless flask lifting and closing
Rebalanced moulding crew sizes from 8 to 5 operators per bay
Deployed Daily Management Systems with shift handover KPI scorecards

clientQuote.text: The industrial engineering work and low-cost hoists transformed our foundry floor. We reduced contract headcount by 35% while increasing casting output.
clientQuote.author: Plant Head, Automotive Casting Foundry

title: CNC Setup & Spindle Optimisation
challenge: Custom machining shop lost 35% of CNC machine capacity to batch setup delays, fixture zero-setting, and CMM inspection waits.
clientSituation: Machinists spending up to 3 hours per batch locating tooling and fixtures
Manual trial-and-error part alignment on 24 CNC machining centers
Frequent delays waiting for CMM quality approval on first-off parts
Low spindle utilization (54%) resulting in missed customer dispatch dates
approach: Conducted setup time analysis across high-precision CNC machining centers
Introduced zero-point modular quick-clamping fixtures for instant part location
Established offline tool presetting routines to prepare tooling before machine stops
Standardized tooling carousels and visual setup instruction sheets
Implemented quick first-off part inspection protocols with dedicated gauge kits
implementation: Equipped 24 CNC machines with standardized zero-point baseplates
Set up a centralized tool presetting room for offline tool measurement
Created visual setup binder checklists for all high-frequency part numbers
Trained machinists on standardized SMED setup procedures

clientQuote.text: By shifting tool presetting offline and introducing zero-point fixtures, our spindle utilization rose from 54% to 76%. We delivered orders faster than ever.
clientQuote.author: Director of Manufacturing, Precision Engineering Plant

title: Fabrication Layout & Lead Time Optimisation
challenge: Heavy structural fabrication facility suffered from crisscrossing overhead crane movements, beam backtracking, and congested welding bays.
clientSituation: Structural steel traveling 3.2 km inside the plant during fabrication
Crisscrossing overhead crane movements creating severe material handling delays
Congested welding bays blocking structural assembly throughput
Long manufacturing lead times tying up working capital in heavy WIP inventory
approach: Created detailed Spaghetti Diagrams tracking overhead crane and plate movement
Analyzed structural steel fabrication steps from cutting to final welding
Designed a unidirectional linear flow layout from plate cutting to dispatch
Established visual WIP buffer bays to regulate material flow between processes
Simulated crane utilization to eliminate crane travel bottlenecks
implementation: Relocated plate cutting machines and welding bays into a linear product bay
Created marked supermarket buffer zones for WIP beam storage
Implemented Kanban signaling for plate movement to welding bays
Trained bay supervisors on visual queue management and daily dispatch targets

clientQuote.text: The redesigned layout significantly improved production flow and reduced unnecessary movement across the shopfloor. Lead time dropped from 21 to 14.7 days.
clientQuote.author: Operations Head, Heavy Structural Fabrication Plant
